Begin a unit of work

Source: R/glow_run_records.R
glow_unit_begin.Rd

Takes the lock of the unit and compares the dependencies of the current run with the completion record in the folder. The result says whether the unit has to run.

glow_unit_begin(
  folder,
  part,
  unit = NULL,
  dependencies,
  force = FALSE,
  level = c("analysis", "dataset")
)

Arguments

folder

The folder of the part (its records are in records/ there).

part

The name of the part.

unit

The name of the unit, such as chr21, or NULL for a part that is not split.

dependencies

The dependencies of the current run: a list of the four named character vectors settings, inputs, files and versions.

force

Logical. TRUE removes an existing record and runs the unit whatever the record states.

level

"analysis" or "dataset". It decides which way forward the refusal names: a new analysis name, or a new dataset name for an asset that belongs to the dataset.

Value

A handle, a list with status and what glow_unit_complete() needs. status is "run" (the unit has to run, and its lock is held) or "complete" (the record states the same dependencies and its outputs exist, and no lock is held).

Details

The overwrite guard: when a record exists and states other settings, outside files or versions, the function stops, prints each difference with the recorded and the current value, and gives the two ways forward. It does so whether or not the recorded outputs still exist. A record that differs in its inputs only is out of date, because a part it read was produced again with the same settings: the unit runs again, and the handle carries the differences in stale. A record whose dependencies are the same and whose outputs are partly gone makes the unit run again.

A unit that runs again first loses its record and then the files that the record lists inside the folder. So the folder never holds a record that describes other results than its files, and a file that the new run does not write (an optional table that was switched off) does not stay behind.

The lock is a folder in records/, <unit>.lock.<n>, that holds a file owner with the host, the process, the SLURM job and a token of the owner. Each acquisition creates the next generation n, complete, and moves it into place in one step, so two runs cannot hold the lock. A released generation keeps its folder, with a file released, so the numbers only grow. A held lock is taken over only when its owner is known to be gone: the process does not exist on this host (or its number was given to another process), or the SLURM job is not in the queue. A scheduler that does not answer proves nothing, and the lock stays. Of several runs that find the same dead owner, one creates the next generation. Any other held lock stops the function with the owner named. Assumption: moving a folder to a name that is free is atomic, and fails when the name is taken by a folder that is not empty, which holds for POSIX file systems. Computational complexity: constant, plus the number of recorded files of a unit that runs again.

The run records (this function, glow_unit_complete(), glow_unit_state(), glow_unit_record(), glow_unit_release(), glow_lock() and glow_seed_unit()) are supported on Linux and macOS, the systems on which the GLOWanalyses templates run. They are not supported on Windows: a record there keeps the full path of an output where it should hold the path below the folder of the unit, so a finished unit is not found complete.

See also

glow_unit_complete(), glow_unit_release()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
h <- glow_unit_begin(folder, "scan", "chr21", dependencies)
if (h$status == "run") {
  # ... the work ...
  glow_unit_complete(h, outputs = file.path(folder, "results", "chr21.csv"))
}
} # }
